unit.why: After a short preface about the tzaddik's many virtues, the narrator tells an event he witnessed himself: he handed the tzaddik a note listing distant strangers by name only, and the tzaddik described each one in detail.

stories.start_quote: אם אמרתי לסדר ולספר אך רק
stories.end_quote: כאילו הכירם מעודם בכל פרטותיהן ודקדוקיהן
stories.summary_en: The narrator gave the tzaddik a kvitl that held only the names and mothers' names of people more than fifty parasangs away whom he had never met, and on reading it the tzaddik described each person's nature and character as if he had always known them.

quotes: האריך הרחיב לתאר ולהעריך כל אחד ואחד
כאילו הכירם מעודם בכל פרטותיהן ודקדוקיהן
tags.why: He knows the character of strangers from their names alone

quotes: בעת שמסרתי לו צעטיל עם כמה שמות בני אדם
tags.why: A kvitl is handed to the rebbe
The story shows the tzaddik's power to act on behalf of petitioners through a kvitl
Told as one example of the tzaddik's spiritual levels (מדריגותיו)

quotes: ממה שקבלתי ממדריגותיו מפי סופרים ומפי ספרים
tags.why: The narrator frames how the tales were passed on to him
